A.input: exact final immutable .kdna container bytes after Core admission
A.normalization: NONE; do not unpack/repack, canonicalize ZIP or remove signature
A.observation: Core computes from the single captured final byte sequence

C.entry_name_rule: Nonempty strict UTF-8 Unicode scalar path, <=4096 bytes, no control/NUL/backslash/absolute/empty/dot/dot-dot segments or trailing slash. Unique exact name bytes; no Unicode normalization. Sort by unsigned UTF-8 bytes.
C.json_entries: Every admitted name ending exactly .json is strict UTF-8 JSON, no duplicate keys at any depth, no invalid Unicode/nonfinite number; RFC8785 JCS bytes. Other admitted entries are binary exact bytes (including payload.kdnab); no guessing by content.
C.manifest_removal_rule: In kdna.json only, remove those properties if present, retain parent objects and every other property. A present /authoring must be an object under Core admission. Never recursively remove another content_digest key.
C.exclusion_rule: checksums/signature are delivery integrity evidence, not content leaves. build-receipt/reports/authoring are forbidden by runtime admission before hashing, not a route for hiding extra entries. All other admitted runtime and attachment entries are included.
C.cycle_rule: C excludes checksums/signature and the two manifest self-references; E can therefore include the final manifest containing C without a C→E→C cycle.
C.framing: ASCII KDNA-CONTENT-TREE + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); for each sorted included entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u8(kind: JSON=0,binary=1) + u64be(contentByteLength) + canonicalJSONorExactBinary. Count/length overflow rejects; never concatenation without framing.

E.input: exact raw entry bytes for kdna.json, payload.kdnab and manifest runtime.mandatory_entries
E.set_rule: New manifest runtime.mandatory_entries is required, a duplicate-free array of valid existing entry names; required base names need not be repeated. Union with the two base entries, sort unsigned UTF-8 bytes. Missing referenced member rejects. Mandatory declarations cannot include checksums.json, signature.kdsig, mimetype or forbidden authoring entries.
E.normalization: NONE: retain raw JSON whitespace/member ordering and exact payload/attachment bytes; set membership comes from admitted manifest, never from checksums expected digest
E.framing: ASCII KDNA-RUNTIME-ENTRY-SET + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); each sorted entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u64be(rawByteLength) + rawBytes. Same entry-name/overflow rules as C.
E.expected_rule: checksums declaration is expected comparison only; cannot supply observed E

P.input: exact complete admitted Runtime Capsule 0.2 object
P.normalization: RFC8785 JCS, strict JSON/Unicode and duplicate-key rejection before object construction
P.self_reference_rule: P is outside Capsule, never embedded and never computed by removing fields.
P.comparison: Producer computes detached P; trusted delivery evidence carries that P; Host independently recomputes P over received Capsule. All three values (producer, delivery, Host observed) must agree before matched; supplied strings do not create a Host observation.

digest_evidence.compared: Both expected and source present; matched iff observed equals expected. Expected is never substituted for observation. Missing actual observation is NOT_EVALUATED in its enclosing technical state, not a fabricated digest.

decisions.chosen: non_schema_rules[].enforcement records only whether the generator machine-checks a rule: IMPLEMENTED_CROSS_ENTRY_CHECK means a machine check exists and the rule id is bound to the implementation's closed id list, and NOT_IMPLEMENTED_NON_SCHEMA means the generator performs no machine check for that rule while stating nothing about runtime enforcement. Per-rule verdicts are DERIVED, not authored: engineering.rule_coverage is a declarative table of facts per rule (machine_checkers: ids of the closed machine-checked list that cover it; generator_uncovered: clauses that machine check leaves out; runtime_units: path[:lines] implementation citations; runtime_uncovered: clauses no runtime in this repository enforces; proof: the gate and case ids that observed the behaviour), and the generator computes generator_machine_check and runtime_enforcement from it as full, partial or none. engineering.runtime_enforcement_claims in the source carries the same two verdicts only as a cross-checked assertion: generation fails when a claim disagrees with the derived value, so a hand-edited verdict cannot survive. The guards that make the facts checkable are: every machine checker id must be in the closed machine-checked list; every runtime unit must be an existing source file with every cited line inside that file's real line count; every proof entry must name a known gate and case ids that exist in that gate; engineering.runtime_not_implemented must be exactly the set of rules with no runtime unit, so no rule can be silently unenforced; and a rule whose machine check is full must be runtime-enforced in full. Current per-rule coverage is generated in public-diagnostics.json. Source case inventory parses real call expressions, excluding comments and strings, but does not assert those calls executed. One residue is explicitly a human judgement and is not presented as machine-guaranteed: the completeness of generator_uncovered and runtime_uncovered, because a claim about what some code does not do cannot be derived from code existence; the machine guarantees only that every such claim is attached to a resolvable citation and that the verdict follows from the declarations.
rejected: reading NOT_IMPLEMENTED_NON_SCHEMA as 'the runtime does not implement this rule'
renaming or deleting the existing enforcement value inside the grammar.2 coordinate (the restricted additive window classifies that as REQUIRES_NEW_COORDINATE)
writing a coverage verdict by hand instead of deriving it, or letting a claim and the derivation disagree
one value standing for two facts, such as a boolean runtime flag that hides a partially covered requirement, or an unnamed subject on a machine-check flag
a citation that only proves a file exists: a directory, a non-source file, a line number past the end of the file, a gate that does not exist, or a case id that gate does not contain
deferred: whether a future coordinate renames the legacy marker
whether a future coordinate adds the runtime mechanisms that would turn the four partial runtime verdicts into full ones
whether the completeness of the uncovered-clause lists can ever be made machine-checkable rather than a reviewed human judgement
basis: window-check.mjs classification of the marker rename as REQUIRES_NEW_COORDINATE
